Was last week’s AI unwind a real washout? This morning’s Nvidia headline is a test, and so far the semis and broader Tech are passing it.

Christophe Barraud’s (@C_Barraud) packed Morning Brief today is full of data on last week’s AI unwind, which many are thinking represented a "washout" of positioning (click through for all of them).

Then over the weekend, Jensen Huang acknowledged in a company-wide memo an affair with a woman reported to be a suspected Chinese intelligence operative. Nvidia, already down 22% from its October high per the Bloomberg chart Barraud flagged, is down another 5.5% in the premarket.

However the groups that took the brunt of last week’s selling aren’t following it lower. The iShares Semiconductor ETF ($SOXX) is up 1.0% premarket, and the Technology Select Sector SPDR ETF ($XLK) is up 0.4%. Both are building on Friday’s bounce: SOXX gained 3.5% and XLK 1.5%. Semis rising while the sector’s bellwether drops 5.5% is the kind of divergence you’d want to see if positioning has fully been cleaned out.

The line in the sand is Thursday’s low: about $131 on SOXX and $162 on XLK. At premarket prices, SOXX has about 5% of cushion above that level and XLK about 2%.

Caveats: premarket trading is thin, and Friday’s bounce faded from the highs, with SOXX hitting $140.21 before closing at $136.53. And unlike April 2025, there’s no policy pivot yet.

After bouncing back last week, Goldman’s Risk Appetite Indicator* fell back to −0.7 from −0.3 the prior week, and the momentum index fell to −1.2 from −0.8, both their lowest since April 2025. Still far from the -1.5 to -2.0 area under which "signals are most powerful"

By component, credit remains the weakest (−2.2), followed by equity volatility (−1.1) and equities (−0.6), while bonds (0.8) and FX & gold (0.5) are still positive.

*”Goldman Sachs Risk Appetite Indicator (RAI) aims to track the level of global market risk appetite and risk aversion based on various market variables. A sharp rise in the index can send a warning signal that investors have more risk appetite and are potentially exposed to a correction if consensus views are tested. Similarly, a sharp decline indicates a reduction in risk appetite, and at extreme levels it can indicate that markets may have overshot. RAI signals are most powerful when the level of risk appetite is very low below -1.5, with levels closer to -2.0 giving the clearest signal over longer time horizons, as at such levels the asymmetry of subsequent medium term equity return becomes very positively skewed. RAI momentum is designed to track short term shifts of market risk appetite, and subcomponents of the RAI.”
